Different models for different groups of strata

Source: R/model-stratified.R
stratified.Rd

Fits one model specification to each group of strata, defined by the levels of a stratum variable, and combines their forecasts into one set of draws. A typical use is a trusted all-cause forecast from one model and cause-specific forecasts from a model that pools sparse causes, reconciled so that the causes add up to all causes:

Usage

stratified(var, ..., .default = NULL)

Arguments

var

Stratum variable that defines the groups.

...

Named model specifications: each name is a level of var whose strata the model is fitted to.

.default

Model for the strata of all other levels (NULL: every level must be named).

Value

A model specification.

Details

reconciled(stratified("cause", all = lee_carter(), .default = li_lee(common_by = c("sex", "cause"))), h, method = "proportional", fixed = all_cause_labels).

Joint models (for example li_lee()) are joint within their group only; the draws of different groups are independent, so sums over strata of different groups have narrower intervals than they would if the groups moved together. reconciled() keeps the draws as they are by default (dependence = "none"). Its dependence = "schaake" reorders the draws of every age, year and stratum so that their ranks follow the observed changes of distinct training years (the Schaake shuffle of Clark et al. 2004, see mt_reconcile()), and dependence = "empirical" reorders the whole paths of each stratum by the observed annual changes of its log age-standardised rate; both also replace the dependence between the strata of a joint group. Each group is fitted and forecast as if it were the whole data, so backtests, anchored(), recalibrated() and reconciled() work as for any model. reconciled(method = "bottom_up") fits its base model to the bottom strata of the hierarchy: named levels that are aggregates of the hierarchy (a total or a group of levels) then have no strata and are skipped.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1990:2019)
spec <- stratified("sex", female = lee_carter(), male = rwd())
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(spec, x), h = 5, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
fc$model
#> [1] "By sex (female: Lee-Carter; male: Random walk with drift)"
